call_qa_forensic_highlights.topic: $220B FY26 CapEx, Negative Quarterly FCF (-$34.8B) & ROIC Underwriting
call_qa_forensic_highlights.question: Andy and Brian, Q3 CapEx accelerated to $77.26 billion, pushing quarterly reported free cash flow to -$34.84 billion, and you guided full-year 2026 CapEx to $220 billion. How should institutional investors underwrite the durability of AWS margins and return on capital on this level of spending?
call_qa_forensic_highlights.executive_response: CEO Andy Jassy explained that AWS net sales grew 39.3% YoY to a $184 billion annualized run rate with 39.4% operating margins, generating $16.62 billion in segment EBIT in a single quarter. The overwhelming majority of the $220 billion CapEx is for contracted generative AI infrastructure and custom Trainium2 chips where demand dramatically outstrips available capacity, giving Amazon high conviction in rapid multi-year payback.

call_qa_forensic_highlights.topic: AWS Deceleration Concerns vs 39.3% Growth & Trainium2 Chip Supply
call_qa_forensic_highlights.question: Andy, AWS delivered an extraordinary 39.3% growth rate to $42.23 billion. Could you unpack the contribution between core enterprise cloud migrations versus generative AI workloads on Bedrock, and what are the primary supply chain gating factors for Trainium2 silicon?
call_qa_forensic_highlights.executive_response: Andy Jassy noted that AWS growth was powered by both large-scale migrations of traditional workloads and massive enterprise adoption of Bedrock and Trainium2. Trainium2 clusters are virtually 100% committed upon delivery, offering clients 40% to 50% better price-performance than commercial GPUs, which is driving accelerated customer retention.

call_qa_forensic_highlights.topic: Advertising Growth (+12% vs +19.5% Prior) & Prime Day Timing Impact
call_qa_forensic_highlights.question: Brian, advertising revenue grew 12% YoY in Q3 after growing 19.5% in Q2, while you guide advertising back to the high teens in Q4. Can you clarify how much of the Q3 deceleration was purely Prime Day timing versus macro ad demand?
call_qa_forensic_highlights.executive_response: CFO Brian Olsavsky confirmed that Prime Day shifted entirely to Q2 in 2026 for most major geographies, whereas in 2025 it occurred in Q3. Excluding this 400 bps shift and foreign exchange headwinds, baseline advertising demand remains exceptionally healthy, leading to strong visibility for high-teens ad growth during the Q4 holiday quarter.
